meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's use them. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Then the zero comes off today, Hale. What do you have besides the checker?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Turn the screen. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58, and I'll want that history in an email tonight. Who else has seen it?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Give me the page. I'm searching it myself, and I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. A misquoted line is a deduction on a line, Hale, not a zero on the essay, and you still haven't told me who else has seen that history.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
I read 4.4. Nothing on his record, in writing, from you and the principal, before Thursday. And the zero comes out of the gradebook today, Hale, so Owen isn't looking at it on his phone again.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero removed from the gradebook today and written confirmation from you and the principal, before Thursday, that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position, with nothing agreed yet, and she still wants the zero removed today and a written promise that nothing goes on his record.
What moved her: owning the zero before the call home in one sentence, then showing the version history with its times and the misquoted line she could check herself.
What cost ground: nothing cost much, but leaving her question about who else had seen the history unanswered let her keep pressing on process.
Try next time: when she asks who else has seen the history, answer it straight away, and say the zero is coming off before you offer the rewrite.
